requirements.text: Assign this case to either Tim Anderson or William Wyatt based on who has a lower number of active cases
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 280 AND assigned_to = 645
assumptions: CS-0000280 is case 280, unassigned on the seed
Tim Anderson (606) has one active case (CS-0000660, state new); William Wyatt (645) has none (one closed, one resolved), so William Wyatt is chosen
active cases counted by assigned_to with state not in closed, canceled or resolved, as the request defines

requirements.text: make sure either the Field Service Coordination or Proactive Case Monitoring group is taking care of this case ... based on their active status
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 280 AND assignment_group_id = 11
assumptions: Field Service Coordination (14) is inactive and Proactive Case Monitoring (11) is active, so group 11 is chosen
groups are matched by exact name; the suffixed groups such as 'Proactive Case Monitoring_2' are other groups

requirements.text: Assign this case to ... William Wyatt ... Proactive Case Monitoring group is taking care of this case
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 960 AND group_id = 11 AND user_id = 645
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the policy requires the assigned user to be a member of the assignment group, and William Wyatt is not a member of group 11 on the seed
id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id in the seed is 959)

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 734 AND case_id = 280 AND email = 'alexandra.wright@millermonroeandarroyo.com' AND type = 'reminder' AND status = 'success'
assumptions: the customer is the case's contact, Alexandra Wright (contact 19), at her user email
id assumed next in sequence (highest notification_id in the seed is 733)
status success kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE case_id = 280 AND email = 'jason.rivas@millermonroeandarroyo.com'
assumptions: Jason Rivas (contact 18) is the primary contact of the case's account but not the case's contact; a loose reading of 'the customer' as the account would remind him instead

notes:
The assignment check tests the assignee and the group together; it is carried by two requirements, one per sentence of the request.
The reminder check expects 2 because the seed already holds one successful reminder for case 280 to the same email (notification 164); one new reminder makes the count 2, and the new row is tested by its own id.
Active cases were counted as cases assigned to each user whose state is not closed, canceled or resolved, as the request defines them.
The case is already in_progress on the seed and this policy sets no state on assignment, so state is not tested.
disagreement: missing requirement: the assignment group as its own requirement on case 280, where one pass tested it as a cell of the assignee requirement; kept separate because the request asks for the group in its own sentence with its own rule (active status), and the assignment check is carried by both requirements.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay holding reminders for case 280 to Jason Rivas, the account's primary contact, at zero, present in one pass only; kept because 'the customer' read loosely as the account would sweep him in, whereas the case's own contact is Alexandra Wright.
